questions.question: In this course, which category of running time is generally considered 'efficient'?
questions.explanation: The lecturer explicitly states that polynomial time is generally what is meant by efficient in this class.
questions.flashcard_front: What is the general definition of an efficient algorithm in this course?
questions.flashcard_back: An algorithm with polynomial running time, denoted as Theta(N^C) for some constant C.
questions.flashcard_explanation: The lecturer identifies polynomial time as the standard threshold for efficiency in this class.

questions.question: Exponential time algorithms are generally considered efficient.
questions.explanation: The lecturer describes exponential time as 'pretty bad' and 'crap' compared to polynomial time.
questions.flashcard_front: Are exponential time algorithms considered efficient?
questions.flashcard_back: False. They are considered inefficient and grow too rapidly.
questions.flashcard_explanation: Exponential growth is significantly faster than polynomial growth, making it inefficient.

questions.question: How does logarithmic time compare to constant time as the input size N becomes very large?
questions.answer: It appears nearly constant and is much closer to constant time than to linear time.
questions.explanation: The lecturer notes that at large scales, log time is much closer to constant than linear, and almost looks like a straight line.
questions.flashcard_front: How does logarithmic time behave at very large input sizes?
questions.flashcard_back: It appears nearly constant and is much closer to constant than linear time.
questions.flashcard_explanation: Logarithmic growth is very slow, making it perform similarly to constant time at scale.

questions.question: Why do we use the Word RAM model in this course?
questions.answer: We use it for its theoretical brevity to define what a computer is allowed to do in constant time.
questions.explanation: The lecturer explains that we need a model to define fundamental operations that take constant time, and Word RAM is used for its theoretical brevity.
questions.flashcard_front: Why is the Word RAM model used?
questions.flashcard_back: For its theoretical brevity in defining constant-time operations.
questions.flashcard_explanation: It provides a standard framework for measuring algorithmic efficiency.
